answer: Lease each applicant one tidal salt pan below a grassy knoll for 120 days, for a 150 token deposit and a 90 dollar license. An anchor marks the pan's seaward corner, and the keeper weighs the brine weekly while a neighbor signs the tally. An inspector checks the pan twice against the stakes. Each weekly entry closes with one fresh line of a sonnet about that pan, so fourteen weeks leave a poem no copyist can fake. A salt pan works like a tide clock, paying only the keeper who shows up when the water comes in. Forging 10,000 pans freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars.
